screen-title.purpose: The title of a top-level screen (Material 3 headline large).

page-title.purpose: The heading of the finished screen and of an empty screen (headline medium).

dialog-title.purpose: The title of a dialog (headline small).

summary.purpose: The line that says what is due today (title large).

deck-name.purpose: A top-level Deck in the deck list (title medium).

deck-name-nested.purpose: A Deck inside another Deck (body large).

study-title.purpose: The Deck path on the study bar (title medium).

answer.purpose: Again, Hard, Good and Easy (title medium).

row-title.purpose: The headline of a row in a list (body large).

lead.purpose: The explanation under a page title (body large).

editor-field.purpose: Editable field content in the Note Editor (body large).

body.purpose: Ordinary interface text and dialog content (body medium).

button.purpose: The label of a button (label large).

count.purpose: A new, learning or due count on the deck list, tabular figures (label large).

study-count.purpose: Remaining counts on the study bar, tabular figures (label large).

caption.purpose: Dates, secondary lines, the time-remaining estimate (body small).

label.purpose: Column headings, navigation labels, answer intervals (label medium).

shadows.name: dialog-scrim

narrative.overview:
Hayaki is a stock Material 3 Android app, finished to the level of Google Calendar, Keep and Tasks. Its look is the category standard and nothing more: one fixed baseline scheme seeded from Baseline Violet, tonal surface containers that group the work, Material's type scale set in the system sans-serif, and the stock control a fluent Android user already trusts wherever one exists. Character comes from finish rather than costume: counts that line up exactly, a progress ring that moves on when a session ends, answer buttons that settle under the thumb.

The density serves someone who studies every day. Many Decks fit on one screen (56dp top-level rows, 48dp nested rows, 8dp between groups), counts never move when a Chinese or Japanese Deck name runs long, and on the study screen the Card Frame recedes so Card Content leads. Anki's own signal colours survive exactly where Anki uses them, on the new, learning and due counts and on the names of the four answers; everything else stays inside the scheme.

The system rejects the paper-and-serif costume of the earlier Quiet paper direction and AnkiDroid's flat table of numbers. It also refuses gamification, a generic template look, few Decks per screen, and motion that slows answering.
keyCharacteristics: One fixed Material 3 scheme seeded from #6750A4, in Light, Dark and Black (true-black surfaces); never wallpaper colour.
Tonal grouping: related rows share one surface container, and groups are separated by space, not lines.
The system sans-serif (Roboto, with the system CJK font for the interface language); hierarchy by size and weight only.
Stock Material 3 controls with the Foundation's shapes and type; custom drawing only for Anki's counts and answers.
Flat at rest: only the add button casts a shadow.
Short, functional motion; nothing between an answer and the next Card takes longer than 120ms.

rules.name: The Fixed Seed Rule
rules.body: One Material 3 scheme seeded from #6750A4, in Light, Dark and Black. Wallpaper dynamic colour is never used, and no surface writes a hex value; it reads a role.

rules.name: The Anki Signal Rule
rules.body: Blue, red, green and amber carry Anki's meanings: new, learning and due, the four answers, and flags. They never decorate. Accents and emphasis stay in the violet scheme.

rules.name: The Earned Pill Rule
rules.body: A count wears its colour and a tinted pill only when there is work to do. A zero is Muted Ink at weight 400 with no pill.

rules.name: The Size-and-Weight Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size and weight only. No style is italic, set in capitals or letter-spaced, and every role sets letter-spacing to 0 in place of Material's default tracking, because Chinese and Japanese have no italics or capitals to fall back on.

rules.name: The System Face Rule
rules.body: Interface text uses the system sans-serif. Any font bundled later must carry the SIL Open Font License, and no interface font ever reaches Card Content.

rules.name: The Group-Not-Hairline Rule
rules.body: Related rows share one surface container with rounded outer corners. Groups are set apart by 8dp of space, and rows inside a group have no dividers.

rules.name: The Still Counts Rule
rules.body: Counts hold their columns whatever the Deck name, language or font size. The name wraps or ends in an ellipsis first.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: The add button and the actions it opens are the only things that cast a shadow. Cards, groups, bars, dialogs and buttons are flat.

rules.name: The Card Frame Rule
rules.body: On the study screen the Card sits on the plain surface inside a flat frame with 12dp corners and a 1dp Hairline stroke. It is the one outlined container, so the Card Frame recedes and Card Content leads.

rules.name: The Stock Control Rule
rules.body: Where Material 3 has the control, use it (Button, FilledTonalButton, TextButton, OutlinedTextField, IconButton, the progress indicators) with the Foundation's shapes and type. Custom drawing is kept for what Anki has and Material does not: count pills and answer buttons.

rules.name: The 120ms Answer Rule
rules.body: Nothing between an answer and the next Card takes longer than 120ms, and an answer press settles in 90ms. With animations turned off in system settings, every motion is instant.

dos: **Do** read every colour by role (`MaterialTheme.colorScheme`, `MaterialTheme.foundation.colors`, `?attr/...`), so Light, Dark and Black all stay right.
**Do** put related rows in one Group Tint container with 16dp outer corners, 8dp from the next group.
**Do** give a screen one filled Baseline Violet button for its main action; other actions are tonal or text buttons.
**Do** keep counts in fixed, aligned columns with tabular figures, and let a long name wrap once, then end in an ellipsis.
**Do** check every surface in English, Simplified Chinese and Japanese; in Light, Dark and Black; right to left; and at 200% font size, with 48dp touch targets and WCAG AA text contrast.
**Do** use Material 3's emphasized decelerate easing (cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1)) for things coming to rest, and keep state changes near 200ms.
donts: **Don't** use wallpaper dynamic colour, add a fourth theme, or write a hex value into a surface.
**Don't** let italics, capitals or letter-spacing carry meaning, and don't carry Material's default tracking onto labels.
**Don't** bundle an interface typeface, and don't restyle Card Content.
**Don't** divide the rows of a group with hairlines; space and container colour do that. Hairlines (1dp) are for dense tables and the card frame.
**Don't** put shadows on cards, groups, bars, dialogs or buttons.
**Don't** use Anki's blue, red, green or amber as decoration or accent.
**Don't** add gamification: streaks, confetti, badges or celebration animation.
**Don't** spend height on oversized Deck cards; the deck list shows many Decks per screen.
**Don't** let any motion between an answer and the next Card run longer than 120ms.
**Don't** bring back the Quiet paper costume: serif or handwritten interface faces, and lists ruled with hairlines instead of grouped.
